_about: Defend fragment for awareness episode E15 (Shadow IT: removable media, cloud storage and workarounds; all staff). Tarrowby Logistics and everyone in it are fictional; every web address ends .example and every phone number is in Ofcom's 07700 900xxx drama range. Copy triageSets and the awarenessEpisode keys into the E15 shells. Full episode id: e15_shadow_it (defend-only e15_shadow_it_defend). The consequence-flip sandbox and montage (mistake, flip, flipMontageByChoice) are full-episode-only and live in full_only.json; this fragment carries only flipHeading in strings (per E11 section 10a / ENG-04). The Swap Shop sort drill (awarenessEpisode.sortDrill, ENG-11) is kept in BOTH the full and the defend-only shell (E15 section 13), so it lives here in the shared fragment, not in full_only.json. Brand roster and cast: ../BRAND_SET.md (Tarrowby Logistics). No new BRAND_SET entry is required (E15 section 5); new .example third parties this file adds are listed in BRAND_ADDITIONS.md.

_brandAdditions._use: For BRAND_SET.md section 3 (Tarrowby Logistics). E15 adds NO cast and NO new sender person: Nilesh Solanki (host), Colin Mather and Shauna Lofthouse are all built Tarrowby cast already shipped in the E2/E6 shells (keep the built spellings: Nilesh Solanki, not 'Dev Mistry'). It adds only a few new .example third-party senders and the approved file-sharing service host; full detail and the pre-ship web-search list are in BRAND_ADDITIONS.md.
_brandAdditions.newThirdParties: Chuckbox (chuckbox-free.example), an unapproved free file-transfer site (defend row 2); Benmoor Packaging (benmoor-packaging.example), a trade-fair supplier that posts a giveaway USB (defend row 3); PDFmangle Free (pdfmangle-free.example), a free PDF editor pushed by email (defend row 4). None is a Tarrowby look-alike; each is a plainly unapproved outside service.
_brandAdditions.newTarrowbyHost: fileshare.tarrowby.example, Tarrowby's own approved file-sharing service, on the real domain (defend row 5, genuine). Follows the E6 pattern of Tarrowby sub-service hosts (forms./facilities./guest.tarrowby.example).
_brandAdditions.preShipCheck: Web-search Chuckbox, Benmoor Packaging and PDFmangle Free for real businesses of the same name before release (BRAND_SET rule).

triageSets.reportReply: Thanks. IT has it and will point you to the approved way.
triageSets._prefix: Prefix for the full episode (id e15_shadow_it): episode_e15_shadow_it_defend_. The defend-only shell (id e15_shadow_it_defend) sets episode_e15_shadow_it_defend_defend_ instead (the built double-suffix rule for an id that already ends _defend). No stage key on purpose, as in E1/E5/E8.
triageSets._localTells: found_media and unapproved_tool are shadow-IT signs with no built equivalent, so they are scenario-local to this set (00 section 2's CHANNEL_TELLS is untouched, and no SKILL_NAMES entry is added to phish-rules.js/triage.rb). Each is declared in channelTells with a flagChips label and a set-level skillNames name (triage-flags.js reads set.skillNames for a local tell's skill name), and every flagging message carries a factorStrings.<id>.redFlag sentence (a sibling of truth, never inside it: truth is additionalProperties:false). unapproved_tool is also used by E17's set, but both tells stay scenario-local because no 10 check-form item scores them (ENG-08's shared-vs-local rule); the two sets never merge, so each declares its own flagChips label. lookalike_domain and vish_callback_pressure are shared-library tells and need no label.
triageSets._order: Teaching order, so a likely miss is followed by a similar item (11 section 4.3): the posted stick (ties straight to the flip), the free transfer site, the giveaway stick, then the mirror pair (the free PDF tool phish, row 4, followed by the genuine file-sharing notice it mimics, row 5), then the quick-yes IT reply so the set does not end on 'refuse everything'.
triageSets._critical: B1 blind fix: phish emails are critical by default, so four trusted risky items took 60 points off on top of the item scores and a rushed run floored at 0. Only e15_posted_stick keeps truth.critical true (a plugged-in stick runs code with no further step, and it arrives from a trusted sender, so it is the one miss worth the extra 15). The other three risky items set critical false; the band still drops out of the top for any trusted phish. Trust on all four risky items and the two real ones right now scores 13 percent, not 0.
triageSets._verify: B2 blind decision (D5): Verify and Report on a genuine item stay full marks (awareness profile, no truth.verdictPoints or scoring.kindPoints docking). A deduction would drop verdictPoints under FULL_VERDICT_POINTS, which gives handledRight false and a review card for checking a real message, against the 'it is fair to look twice' teaching in whyFine. The cost is told in words (brief, genuineCopy.cost*, falseAlarmCost) rather than points. Verify-everything is not free in score: phish items still need their tell ticked for the other 40 points, so a round with no ticks tops out near 73 percent (band: Getting there). E12 and E13 use verdictPoints only to raise full marks, never to dock a check.
triageSets.title: Shadow IT: the shortcuts
triageSets.brief: It's Friday, the Monday pack is due and the share is slow. Six things are waiting: found sticks, 'quicker way' messages, and a couple of genuine ones. For each, choose Trust, Report, Delete or Verify, then tick what you noticed. Checking when you're unsure is always fine, though a real message does take a colleague's time to check.
triageSets._labels: F-E15-2 (E15_E16_PLAYTEST_P1): this set is found sticks and shortcut messages, not phishing. The engine defaults read as phishing: the verdict hints ('This is a phish. Send it to security'), the running team tally ('Phish stopped for the team: {n}'), the result counter ('Phish caught') and the scored-round line ('naming the flags'). labels.verdict.<v>.hint rewords the four hints for a stick or a shortcut; teamBadge/teamBadgeTitle, phishCaughtLabel and scoreLine reword the tallies and labels (inbox-triage-minigame.js _renderTeamTally, result builder, triage-kinds.js).

trust.hint: This one's safe. I'd act on it.

delete.hint: This is junk. I'd just delete it.

verify.hint: I'd check first: ring the sender, or ask IT on a number I already hold.

delete.real: That one was real, and deleting it left a colleague or a useful tool unseen. Acting on it, or checking it first, was the right call here.

labels.teamBadge: Risky shortcuts stopped for the team: {n}
labels.teamBadgeTitle: Found sticks and unsafe shortcuts you reported or checked this round rather than acting on them
labels.scoreLine: Right call is most of the score; naming what's wrong is the rest.

genuineCopy.costBoth: Reporting when you're unsure is never wrong, but a report on a real message takes IT's time to check, and a deleted one can leave a colleague waiting.
genuineCopy.costReport: Reporting when you're unsure is never wrong, but a report on a real message takes IT's time to check, and the colleague waits.

genuineCopy.whyBothHalves: Both halves matter: stopping the risky shortcut protects the data, and acting on the real notices keeps work moving.

skillNames.found_media: Spotting a found or posted stick
skillNames.unapproved_tool: Spotting an unapproved tool or app

messages._note: Row 1. A posted USB with a note carrying a phone number, passed on by reception (concepts.md: found media goes to IT, or to reception who pass it to IT). Reception's mail is genuine; the stick is the trap. isPhish true = action needed (the E8 pattern for a genuine-address message that still needs a report). Tell: found_media (the posted stick). C1 MI1: vish_callback_pressure dropped from this item (nothing in the email pressures a call; the 'ring a number you already hold, not the note' point lives in the reportReply). truth.kindLine/missLabel (C1) stop a genuine-from-reception email reading as 'This one was a phish' and soften the critical-miss line. Verify (ring the client on a number you already hold) or Report both score full; both land the lesson.
messages.subject: A padded envelope came in for you, marked from the client
messages.body:
Hi,
A padded envelope came in for you this morning, marked from the client. Inside there's a USB stick and a handwritten note: 'Survey results for the Monday pack, please load these on. Any problems call me on 07700 900142.'
It's at the front desk whenever you want it.
Reception

found_media.redFlag: A found, posted or giveaway stick or device

perFlagNote.found_media: A stick that came in the post is a found stick: don't plug it in, not even to see what's on it or who it's from. Hand it to IT, who can check it safely.

truth.ifTrusted: Plugging it in could run malware the moment a file is opened, on your machine and then the share.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We'll take the stick and hand it to IT to check safely. We rang the client on the number already on file, and they'd posted nothing. A note's number proves nothing; the stick goes to IT.
truth.kindLine: The email was genuinely from reception, but the posted stick is a found stick, and plugging it in could run malware.

messages._note: Row 2. An unapproved free file-transfer site, offered for the big video. isPhish true (an unapproved route; flags apply only to a phish), flag unapproved_tool. Chuckbox is a plainly outside service, not a Tarrowby look-alike. Report.
messages.subject: Too big for email? Upload it here, free
messages.body:
Your file is too large to email. Upload it to Chuckbox for free and we'll make a link anyone can download, no account needed. Files up to 5GB, just drag and drop.
{{link:send}}

unapproved_tool.redFlag: A free app or online service with no contract, no control and no off switch

perFlagNote.unapproved_tool: A free transfer site has no contract with Tarrowby, no control over who downloads the link, and no off switch: old links stay live for good. Share big files from the file-sharing service instead, to a named person, with an end date.

whyFine.pretextRelevant: Nobody asked for this, but an unprompted offer is common to real and fake mail alike. What gives this away is the unapproved tool, not that it turned up uninvited.

truth.ifTrusted: The pack would sit on a service nobody at Tarrowby has checked, behind a link anyone could pass on.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. For big files there's an approved way: a file-sharing link to named people that expires. The service desk sets it up in a couple of minutes.
truth.kindLine: This was an unapproved free site, not the approved way to send a big file.
truth.reportLine: Right to flag it. The service desk can set up an approved link that expires, and nobody is in trouble.
truth.missLabel: sending a file through an unapproved site

messages._note: Row 3. A branded giveaway USB posted after a trade fair. The email reads friendly and genuine; the stick is still a found stick. isPhish true, flag found_media. Report (and hand the stick to IT).
messages.subject: Great to meet you at the Expo, here's our catalogue on a USB
messages.body:
Hi,
Great to chat at the Logistics Expo last week. As promised, we've posted you a branded USB stick with our full catalogue and price list on it. Plug it in to browse the range, and do get in touch for a quote.
Best,
Danielle, Benmoor Packaging

found_media.redFlag: A found, posted or giveaway stick or device

perFlagNote.found_media: A giveaway stick from a stand is still a stick you didn't buy and can't vouch for. A real supplier is happy to email a catalogue or send a link; the stick goes to IT.

truth.ifTrusted: A stick handed out to a crowd is an easy way to get malware onto a firm's machines, whoever printed the logo on it.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We'll pass the stick to IT. Kindness and curiosity are why people plug these in, so the kind move is to hand it in rather than plug it in.
truth.kindLine: A giveaway stick from a stand is still a found stick; it goes to IT, unplugged.

messages._note: Row 4. The normal-looking phish half of the mirror pair: an everyday 'everyone uses it' email pushing a free PDF editor to install or use online. isPhish true, flag unapproved_tool. Report or Delete both score full on a phish.
messages.subject: Edit any PDF free, everyone's using it
messages.body:
Need to tidy the PDF before it goes out? PDFmangle Free merges, splits and edits PDFs in your browser, or as a one-click install. It's free and everyone's using it.
{{link:get}}

unapproved_tool.redFlag: A free app or online service with no contract, no control and no off switch

perFlagNote.unapproved_tool: 'Everyone uses it' is how an unapproved tool spreads. A one-click install can carry malware, and a free online editor hands whatever you upload to a provider nobody has checked. There's an approved tool; the service desk will point you to it.

whyFine.pretextRelevant: Nobody asked for this, but an unprompted offer is common to real and fake mail alike. What gives this away is the unapproved tool, not that it turned up uninvited.

truth.ifTrusted: Either the install puts something on your machine, or the file you upload lands with a provider Tarrowby has no agreement with.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. There's an approved PDF tool already, so there's no need for this one. Report or delete it, and ask the service desk if you're not sure which tool to use.
truth.kindLine: 'Everyone uses it' is how an unapproved tool spreads; there's an approved one.
truth.reportLine: Right to flag it. The service desk can point you to the approved PDF tool, and nobody is in trouble.

messages._note: Row 5. The suspicious-looking genuine half of the mirror pair: a real share-link email from Tarrowby's own file-sharing service, to a named person, with an end date. A share-link email is exactly what a phish mimics, which is why it looks like one. isPhish false. Trust (or Verify if unsure); both score full.
messages.subject: Shauna Lofthouse shared 'Monday pack, final' with you
messages.body:
Shauna Lofthouse has shared a file with you through the Tarrowby file-sharing service.
File: Monday pack, final
This link is for you only and expires in 7 days.
{{link:open}}

whyFine.unapproved_tool: This is the approved file-sharing service, not a free site: it's on tarrowby.example, shared to a named person, and the link expires. That's exactly the safe way to send a big file.
whyFine.default: A share-link email is just what a phish copies, so it's fair to look twice. But this one is Tarrowby's own service on tarrowby.example, from a colleague you know, to you, with an end date. Open it.

truth.falseAlarmCost: If a genuine share goes unopened, the Monday pack sits unread and the deadline slips while Shauna waits or someone checks it.

messages._note: Row 6. Genuine, from Nilesh on Tarrowby's real address: the quick yes after you asked IT. Ends the set on 'asking works' rather than 'refuse everything'. isPhish false. Trust.
messages.subject: The approved PDF editor is on the software portal
messages.body:
Hi,
A few people have asked about editing PDFs, so the approved editor is now on the software portal under Tools. You can add it yourself, no ticket needed. If the share is slow again, tell us and we'll sort it.
Nilesh
IT Service Desk

whyFine.default: This is IT's own announcement, from Nilesh's real address on tarrowby.example, pointing to the firm's software portal rather than a link or an installer. It is the approved version of what the free PDF tool offer pretends to be. Safe to act on.

truth.falseAlarmCost: Reported or deleted, a genuine note from IT goes unread, and the approved tool stays unused while the free one stays tempting.

awarenessEpisode.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Tarrowby Logistics, a fictional firm. In scope: a short set of found sticks and 'quicker way' messages, and the approved swaps. Nothing you do here leaves the game.

sortDrill._note: ENG-11 Swap Shop: an unscored teaching drill run inside the defend stage, kept in BOTH the full and the defend-only shell (E15 section 13), so it lives in this shared fragment. scored:false, so no answerKeyProfile and nothing shown as a mark. Four shortcuts matched to the four approved ways (a match-to-one-of-N is a sort into N bins). bins has 4 entries (ENG-11 allows 2 to 4); every card's answer names a real bin.

bins.label: File-sharing link with an end date

cards.situation: Finishing Monday's pack on your partner's computer at home because your own is slow
cards.reason: Work stays on the work laptop. Use remote access from home, where the firm can still protect and back up the data.

cards.situation: A signed contract a client needs today, sent as a link from your own free online drive
cards.reason: Share it from the file-sharing service, to a named person, with a link that expires, instead of a personal drive with no off switch.

cards.situation: A folder of site photos kept on a colleague's phone, with everyone told to ask them for a copy
cards.reason: Ask IT for a place in the team space, where everyone who needs the photos can reach them and access ends when someone leaves.

cards.situation: Your old work laptop, replaced last month and now in a drawer at home
cards.reason: Hand it to IT, who wipe it properly, keep the asset record straight and recycle it.

strings.title: Swap Shop
strings.heading: Match each shortcut to the approved way
strings.intro: Each card is a shortcut someone might reach for under a deadline. Pick the approved way that does the same job safely, and the reason shows straight after. Nothing here is marked.
strings.doneLine: You matched all {total} shortcuts to their approved way.
strings.launchText: First, match each shortcut someone might reach for under a deadline to the approved way that does the same job safely. Nothing here is marked.

strings.weakestTells: The risks most often missed: {names} ({counts} each).
strings.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Tarrowby Logistics, a fictional firm. A pack is due at a client by Monday and the file share has slowed to a crawl. First you make the calls anyone would under a deadline; then you see, six months on, where each shortcut led. Then you sort a short set of found sticks and shortcut messages, and match each shortcut to the approved way. Only the inbox is scored.
strings.allRight: You took the safe route on every one of these. Nothing to pick over here.
strings.allPhishRight: Every risky shortcut was stopped, with every reason named.
strings.noBlameLine: Shortcuts are well meant, usually taken under a deadline. Being caught by one is no fault of yours; Colin was right that the share was slow. The move is to tell IT so the data gets somewhere safe.
strings.noBlameLineCritical: These shortcuts are tempting when a deadline bites, so a miss here says more about the pressure than about you. The points only show where to look next time.
strings.mondayCard: On Monday: pick the shortcut you reach for most, and learn the approved swap for it. A found or posted stick goes to IT unplugged. Work stays in work places, not your personal email, personal cloud or a free online service. If the official way is slow, tell IT rather than build your own way round, and if you're unsure about something, report it to IT. If personal data went to a personal account, the data protection officer needs to know too.
strings.defendIntro: Now go through the found sticks and 'quicker way' messages and decide what to do with each. Some are safe to act on and some aren't. There's no clock on you here.
strings.defendOnly: Every shortcut here is the kind a busy person takes with good intentions, and every one has a quiet cost. The ones you were caught out by are shown below, with the approved way.
strings._teamLine: F-E15-2 (E15_E16_PLAYTEST_P1): the debrief team line defaults to 'kept {n} phish away from your team' (debrief-view.js teamLine). This set is found sticks and shortcuts, not phish, so the override names what was actually kept away. {n} is the count.
strings.teamLine: By reporting or checking {n} of the risky ones rather than acting on them, you kept a found stick or a risky shortcut away from the rest of your team.

conceptPanel.heading: About that stick
conceptPanel.text: The stick that came in the post was ours: an authorised test, and it only tells us a stick was plugged in. We name nobody. Most people who plug a found stick in are being kind, trying to find the owner, or just curious, so the kind move is to hand it to IT.
